cards.explanation: The answer is False, friends. Mark says Jesus entered the house not wanting anyone to know He was there, but He "…was unable to escape their notice." (Mark 7:24) Word got around anyway. A house with a secret in it is a lot like a bakery with a fresh batch in it, because somebody always finds out.

The answer is she falls at His feet, friends. Mark says she heard about Jesus, "…and she came and fell at His feet." (Mark 7:25) She ended up right at His feet. I think that tells you how much her little girl mattered to her.

The answer is False, friends. Mark says she "…kept asking Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter." (Mark 7:26) That's not one polite question and a wave goodbye. She kept on asking, and I think that's one stubborn kind of love.

The answer is that even the dogs under the table eat the crumbs, friends. She answers, "Yes, Lord," and then adds, "even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs." (Mark 7:28) She takes what Jesus said and answers right inside it. I can't answer anybody that well even when I get three days to think.

The answer is that the demon has left her daughter, friends. Jesus says, "Because of this answer, you may go. The demon has left your daughter." (Mark 7:29) He says it as already done. Mark tells us the woman went home and found her child lying on the bed, and the demon was gone (Mark 7:30).

The answer is True, friends. Mark says the woman "…went home and found her child lying on the bed, and the demon was gone." (Mark 7:30) What Jesus told her was exactly what she found. I think that's one very good homecoming.

The answer is that they beg Jesus to place His hand on him, friends. Mark says the people "…begged Jesus to place His hand on him." (Mark 7:32) They brought the man to Jesus and begged for exactly that. I think bringing someone to Jesus like that shows how much they cared about him.
The answer is False, friends. Mark says Jesus "…took him aside privately, away from the crowd…" (Mark 7:33) The crowd stayed back. I think a quiet spot has its own kind of kindness.

The answer is his ears and his tongue, friends. Mark says Jesus "…put His fingers into the man’s ears. Then He spit and touched the man’s tongue." (Mark 7:33) The man was deaf and hardly able to speak, and those are the two places Jesus touched. Those touches matched the two troubles the man had.

The answer is opened, friends. Jesus says, "Ephphatha!" and Mark adds, "(which means, 'Be opened!')" (Mark 7:34) One word and nothing else. Right after, Mark says the man's ears were opened and his tongue was released (Mark 7:35).

The answer is True, friends. Mark says, "Immediately the man’s ears were opened and his tongue was released, and he began to speak plainly." (Mark 7:35) He didn't have to wait around or practice. He went from deaf to hearing and speaking plainly.

The answer is that the more He orders them, the more they tell it, friends. Mark says, "But the more He ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it." (Mark 7:36) The harder Jesus pushed for quiet, the louder the news got. That's how good news goes.

The first blank is hear and the second blank is speak, friends. The people say, "He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!" (Mark 7:37) Hear is exactly what the deaf man got to do, because his ears were opened (Mark 7:35). Speak is what his tongue was released to do, and he began to speak plainly (Mark 7:35). The people's astonishment came out in those words.
